# I1
Verdict: strong-accept
CRITICAL: 0
MAJOR: 0
Headline: Within the stipulated synthetic universe, E5 supplies an analytic basis for a novel continuation-preserving memory mechanism, and candidate.json provides a discriminating first-paper experiment.
Occupation: E1 already occupies synchronous partial-order compression and O(w log n) frontier storage; E2 occupies delayed-outcome belief updates. The attributable difference is preserving safe continuations while compressing dependencies involving pending outcomes, which neither record supplies (E1, E2, E5). The complete full-method coverage and low combined-mechanism overlap stipulated in prior_work.md support novelty only within this hypothetical universe.
Experiment: candidate.json proposes exact continuation comparisons across six graphs with 6–12 actions, followed by 1,200 paired interruption seeds across 30 unseen graphs, three training seeds, and two delay levels. It includes the mandatory strongest E3/E4 baselines, full-log and no-memory references, frozen perception/control, matched budgets, and separate pending-tracking and merging ablations. False-safe continuations immediately falsify the safety claim; the paired-interval rule explicitly tests the proposed five-percentage-point benefit. E6 supplies enumeration and deterministic replay. Finite enumeration does not discharge the general theorem obligation acknowledged in candidate.json.
Estimand: Unsafe-continuation episodes divided by all interrupted episodes, assessed at matched completion and jointly with memory bytes, aligns with the proposed memory/error payoff (candidate.json). Reporting completion alongside safety addresses apparent gains obtained by completing fewer tasks; byte accounting tests storage beyond the event-identifier bound.
Payoff: E5 establishes that identical event multisets and marginal outcome probabilities can conceal different safe continuations when pending execution interacts with contact dependencies. This specifically motivates retaining joint pending/dependency information. E1 supports compression of independent completed actions, while E2 supports late-feedback tracking; their verified limitations motivate the adaptation. E6 makes compact memory operationally necessary and supplies dependency labels. These premises support a prospective attributable payoff; they do not establish the proposed algorithm’s correctness or measured improvement.
Feasibility: The proposed two-researcher plan uses 8,000 trajectories, frozen perception/control, two A100 GPUs, 48 GPU-hours, and CPU enumeration (candidate.json). This is a credible bounded first-paper scope under the supplied simulator capabilities (E6), although the runtime allocation remains a proposal rather than a measured result.
History: unavailable
Reason: Strong accept is justified under review_contract.md by the complete conditional coverage in prior_work.md, the independently supported gap and causal witness in E1/E2/E5, the external constraint in E6, and candidate.json’s feasible experiment with strongest baselines, attribution controls, and explicit kill conditions; the unproved theorem and unrun experiments remain research obligations rather than established results.
